turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Mr. Hale, before the doctor steps in, I need to flag your blood pressure. Just now it was 168 over 94, and I put that in the chart.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): 168? That's bad, right? I only came about my knee and a form for work. Am I about to have a stroke sitting here?
[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): You're talking a mile a minute, which doesn't help. I'll repeat it in a minute. Just stay seated.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ugh, this computer ate the last screen. What did you come in for? Say it slow, I clicked the wrong encounter.
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): A form for the warehouse. My left knee's been aching and they won't put me on light duty without a note. That's the whole visit, or it was.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Knee, warehouse, a note. Give me the knee part again? The window refreshed and I lost it.
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Left knee. It aches, worse on the dock stairs. I don't think it's swollen. I just need the paper so I don't lose the shift.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Got it. Maya, where'd the pressure land? I can't find the vitals row.
[SEG0009] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): First reading, 168 over 94. I rechecked the other arm just now, 176 over 102.
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): 176 over 102? That's worse. This is the white coat thing, it always jumps in a clinic. At the pharmacy it was fine, I swear. Am I in danger this minute?
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): When was that pharmacy check, and what number did they get?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): I can't date it. Last winter, or the one before. I didn't write it down. Maybe one thirty something, I honestly don't know.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): So no usable home number. Any chest pain, headache, or change in your vision today?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No chest pain, no headache, eyes are fine. I'm just scared because my dad had a stroke. That's why this is frying me.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Your dad had a what? Something dinged, say it again.
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): A stroke. Years back. They had him on a pile of pills after, and I don't want that life.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Okay. With 176 over 102 I'm starting lisinopril, ten milligrams, once a day, today. I'll send it while this loads.
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Today? Forever? What if it tanks and I can't drive home? Is ten a lot? My neighbor's on five. Are you even looking at me or at the screen?
[SEG0019] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Want a clean repeat before a script goes out? He was mid-sentence on the first one.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yeah. Read me the second set again. I typed 167 and that looks wrong.
[SEG0021] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): 176 over 102. Not 167.

[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): And for the knee I've been living on ibuprofen. Four hundred milligrams... no, six hundred, the big tablets. I almost said two of them, but it's one six-hundred tablet, twice a day, after work.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Six hundred, twice a day. How long has the knee been doing this?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): I can't put a date on it. The ache has been there since last winter, or the winter before that. It crept up. Some days it's nothing.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Stairs make it worse? Sorry, I was scrolling.
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, stairs, and standing on the concrete the whole shift. Sitting in the break room eases it off. No giving way, no locking.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Is the form going to say high blood pressure? HR will panic and I need those hours. Can you write the knee and leave the pressure off? Please?
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): The form is the knee and light duty. I'm not diagnosing hypertension off two readings in a nervous visit. Hang on, the order screen popped.

[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Actually, scratch the lisinopril. No tablets today. You might be white coat, you might have real hypertension, and without a written home number I'm not starting a pill on two clinic readings. We'll do home monitoring instead.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): No pill? You're sure? What if it's still up tonight and I stroke in my sleep the way my dad did? Should someone stay with me?

[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Chest pain, a bad headache, or weakness on one side, that's the ER, not your couch. Otherwise we watch it at home. I'm opening the cuff-loan page, this portal is crawling.
[SEG0032] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): We can loan a cuff from the front desk. Morning and evening for two weeks, write both numbers, and I'll print a log sheet.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do that. Bring the log back in two weeks and we'll decide if this is real.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks, both times a day. What if my machine's cheap and lies? Do I use both arms? And can I keep the ibuprofen or is that dangerous with this pressure?
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): Left arm each time, sit five minutes first. Keep the ibuprofen, six hundred twice a day, with food. Don't add any other pain pill.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): With food, okay. Are you actually signing the form, or is that stuck in the computer too? I keep asking, I know, I'm rattled.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll sign the light-duty note before you go. Two weeks light duty, no ladders, nothing over twenty pounds. Now where did the cuff checkbox go.

[SEG0038] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Side note, the 405 was a parking lot this morning. I left at six-thirty and still walked in late. Almost missed my granddaughter's recital last night, the little one on triangle, convinced she was the star.

[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Triangle kids are the best. My grandson had a drum at preschool and mostly just yelled into it. We sat in the lot after while the rain came sideways, and he narrated every drop.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): Rain's parked over us through Thursday, apparently. I burned twenty minutes hunting a spot and paid eight bucks in the garage. Eight bucks to park at my own building.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Eight bucks is a crime. I took surface streets and caught every red from Sepulveda down. Then the ice cream place was closed, so the whole evening was a bust.
[SEG0042] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Next recital, ice cream is guaranteed, closed or not. I'll go print that log. You two wrap the medical part.

[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yeah, Thursday rain, thrilling. Alright, chart's back. I was going to order a knee x-ray, but watching you bend it just now, no: no swelling, and the bend is full. This is a strain, not something I need a picture of today.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): A strain. No picture, no pill. What number at home means I shouldn't wait the two weeks? I keep seeing my dad's face, I'm sorry.

[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): If the top number stays over 180, or those warning symptoms come back, don't wait. Otherwise two weeks is the plan. If the log looks ugly we can talk about a pill then, not before.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Over 180, don't wait. And the form really won't mention the pressure? Say it one more time, I won't relax until I hear it twice.
[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): Work note is knee and light duty only. The pressure stays in our chart, off the form. Repeat the restrictions so I know they stuck.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks light duty, no ladders, nothing over twenty pounds. Left knee. Blood pressure log in two weeks, morning and night.
[SEG0049] person_3 (DOCTOR): That's it. Cuff and log are at the front desk under your name. Drive easy, it's still wet out there.

doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats
